newsitem.title: FRANCE: Legras sees long negotiations on EU farm reform.
newsitem.headline: Legras sees long negotiations on EU farm reform.

text.p: The European Union's senior permanent farm official on Monday predicted lengthy negotiations between member states before the EU's latest farm reform plan can be finalised.
The European Commission last week unveiled proposals for price-cutting reforms, labelled Agenda 2000, to prepare for expansions eastwards and prevent the return of surpluses.
European Commission agriculture director-general Guy Legras told reporters in Paris he expected the full process of preparation and negotiation to take at least 18 months.

"I think if it is done by the end of 1998 then it will be an achievement," he said. He noted a previous reform which forms the basis for current policies took around the same time to negotiate between February 1991 and May 1992.

The latest proposals have run into opposition from French, German and other farmers who stand to see support prices for dairy products, beef and grain slashed by up to 30 percent around the turn of the century.
